source: Hebrew Gospel of Luke v2.1 (Van Rensburg 2026, Vat. Ebr. 100)
method: Consonantal analysis — niqqud stripped, no English/Greek reference provided

verses.translation: It came to pass that when many people [or: crowds] came to him so that they might hear the word of YHWH, he was standing close to the lake [or: river] of Gennesaret
words: in order that / on account of

translation_notes: היה (H-Y-H): Candidates: H1961 'to exist/become/come to pass', H1962 'ruin'. Chose H1961 because the context describes an event unfolding ('it came to pass').
כאשר (K-ʾ-Sh-R): The כ prefix + אשר; candidates for אשר include H834 'who/which/when'. Chose H834 as temporal conjunction 'when' because it introduces a temporal clause.
בעבור (B-ʿ-B-W-R): Candidates: H5668 'on account of / in order that', H5669 'stored grain'. Chose H5668 because purpose clause follows ('that they would hear').
דבר (D-B-R): Candidates: H1696 'to speak', H1697 'word/matter', H1698 'pestilence', H1699 'pasture'. Chose H1697 'word' because it is the object of 'hear' and paired with YHWH.
והוא (W-H-W-ʾ): Candidates: H1931 'he', H1933 'to be'. Chose H1931 'he' as the emphatic pronoun introducing a new clause about the subject standing.
textual_notes: נעשה has no candidates listed; the consonants could be niphal of עשה ('it was done/made') or cohortative qal ('let us make'). Context (narrative past) strongly favors niphal passive 'it was done/it happened'.
יאור has no candidates listed; standard Hebrew יאור (H2975) means 'river/Nile/stream'. Here paired with Gennesaret it refers to the lake/body of water.
עמים could be H5971 'peoples' (plural) or the ים-intensified form. Context ('many') supports numerical plural: 'many people'.
]גניסר[ is bracketed in the source, indicating an editorial note or uncertain reading. It is a proper noun (Gennesaret/Kinnereth).

verses.literal: It was done [that] it happened when peoples many came to him in order that they would hear [the] word [of] YHWH and he [was] standing near [the] river [of] Gennesaret

verses.translation: And he saw two boats [or: vessels] beside the lake, and the men [or: fishermen] had gone out from them and were washing the nets

translation_notes: וראה (W-R-ʾ-H): Candidates: H7200 'to see', H7201 'vulture', H7203 'seer/vision'. Chose H7200 because the waw-consecutive + verb form fits narrative: 'and he saw'.

שתי (Sh-T-Y): Candidates: H8358 'intoxication', H8359 'warp in weaving'. Neither fits. The consonants שתי also represent the feminine construct of שנים/שתים ('two'). Context (counting boats) demands 'two'.
textual_notes: שתי is listed with H8358 'intoxication' and H8359 'warp', but the word is clearly the feminine construct numeral 'two' (שתי from שתים), which may lack a separate Strong's entry in the provided candidates. Context unambiguously requires 'two'.
אףניות has no Strong's candidates. The consonants suggest a loanword or late Hebrew form for 'boats/ships' (cf. ספינה). The narrative context (lake, nets, fishermen) confirms 'boats'.

verses.literal: And he saw two boats near the river and the men went out and [were] washing the nets

verses.translation: And he went up into one of the boats, which belonged to Shimon, and asked [or: requested] him to push the boat out from the water [or: shore] a little. Then he sat down and [began] teaching the people [or: crowd] from the boat

translation_notes: עלה (ʿ-L-H): Candidates: H5927 'to ascend/go up', H5928 'holocaust', H5929 'leaf', H5930 'burnt offering', H5931 'pretext'. Chose H5927 because the action of boarding a boat is 'going up into' it.
ומבקש (W-M-B-Q-Sh): H1245 'to search out/request'. The מ prefix indicates participle; context (asking someone to do something) fits 'requesting'.
מעט (M-ʿ-T): Candidates: H4591 'to lessen', H4592 'a little', H4593 'sharp'. Chose H4592 'a little' because it modifies the distance of moving the boat.
ומלמד (W-M-L-M-D): Candidates: H4451 'oxgoad', H3925 'to teach'. The מ prefix suggests participle of למד; chose H3925 'teaching' because the scene describes him instructing the people.
לעם (L-ʿ-M): Candidates: H5971 'people/tribe', H5973 'with'. Chose H5971 because the ל prefix + עם as 'to the people' fits the teaching context.
אשר (ʾ-Sh-R): Chose H834 'who/which/that' as relative pronoun connecting 'people' to 'in the boat'.
textual_notes: מ<מעון appears to be a damaged or abbreviated form. The < likely represents a missing letter. Given H8095 שמעון (Shimon) appeared in section 4 for לשמעון, this is likely 'of Shimon' with the שׁ partially missing or abbreviated.
מ<ם similarly appears damaged; context suggests 'from the water' (מן + מים) or 'from there' (מן + שם). Given the boat-on-water scene, 'from the water/shore' is most natural.
שיסיע has no candidates; the root may be נסע ('to travel/move/pull up') in hiphil with ש prefix ('that he would move/push off'), fitting the request to move the boat from shore.
The final באףניה could mean 'in the boat' (from the boat) or 'from the boat' depending on whether we read ב as locative. Context of teaching from the boat favors 'from the boat'.

verses.literal: And he went up in [the] boat one that was of Shimon and requesting him that he move the boat from the water a little and he sat and teaching the people who [were] in the boat

verses.translation: And when he had finished speaking, he said to Shimon: Take [or: lead] the boat out into the deep water [or: sea], and spread out [or: scatter] your nets in it [for a catch]
words: in the sea / into the water

translation_notes: וכאשר: כ + אשר H834 'when' — temporal conjunction introducing a completed action.
לדבר (L-D-B-R): Candidates: H1696 'to speak', H1697 'word', H1698 'pestilence', H1699 'pasture'. Chose H1696 because the ל prefix + infinitive 'to speak' follows 'finished'.
אמר (ʾ-M-R): Candidates: H559 'to say', H561 'something said', H563 'lamb'. Chose H559 'he said' because it introduces direct speech.
לשמעון: H8095 'Shimon' — proper name, the person being addressed.
בים (B-Y-M): Candidates: H3220 'sea/large body of water', H3222 'warm spring'. Chose H3220 because the Gennesaret lake context fits 'sea/deep water'.
textual_notes: סיים has no candidates provided; it appears to be a late Hebrew/Mishnaic form meaning 'he finished/completed' (from root סים/סיים).
תוליך has no candidates; it is likely hiphil imperfect of הלך or ילך ('you shall cause to go / take / lead'), fitting the command to move the boat.
ופזרו has no candidates; root פזר means 'to scatter/spread', fitting the action of casting nets.
]בלקיחה[ is bracketed, indicating editorial uncertainty. It appears to mean 'for a catch/taking' from root לקח ('to take/catch').

verses.literal: And when he finished to speak he said to Shimon take the boat into the sea and scatter the nets in it [for a catch]

verses.translation: And Shimon answered and said to him: All [through] the night we have toiled [or: labored] and we have not caught a thing [or: anything]. But at your word, we will cast out [or: extend] your nets
words: in your words / at your word

translation_notes: ענה (ʿ-N-H): Candidates: H6030 'to respond/answer', H6031 'to depress/afflict', H6034 'Anah (name)'. Chose H6030 because the pattern 'answered and said' is a standard Hebrew narrative formula.
ואמר: H559 'to say' — continues the speech formula.
דבר (D-B-R): Candidates: H1697 'word/thing/matter', H1696 'to speak', H1698 'pestilence', H1699 'pasture'. Chose H1697 as 'thing' because after 'we did not catch' it means 'not a thing / nothing'.
אבל (ʾ-B-L): Candidates: H56 'to bewail', H57 'lamenting', H58 'meadow', H61 'nay/truly/yet'. Chose H61 'but/yet' because it introduces a contrast between failure and willingness to try again.
textual_notes: טרחנו has no candidates; root טרח means 'to labor/toil' in later Hebrew. The first person plural past form fits the context of fishermen describing their night's work.

נאריך has no candidates; it appears to be hiphil first person plural of ארך ('to lengthen/extend'). In context, 'extending nets' means casting or spreading them. Alternatively, it may be a variant for 'we will cast/let down'.
רשתותיך — 'your nets' with 2ms possessive suffix. Interesting that Shimon says 'your nets' rather than 'our nets', possibly deferring ownership of the action to the one commanding.

verses.literal: And Shimon answered and said to him all the night we labored and not we caught a thing but in your words we will extend your nets

verses.translation: And when this was done, they gathered [or: collected] a great [quantity of] fish — so many that their nets were breaking [or: tearing apart]

translation_notes: זה (Z-H): Candidates: H2088 'this/that', H2089 'sheep', H2090 'this/that'. Chose H2088 because 'this' as demonstrative pronoun refers back to the action of casting nets.
שלהם: The ש prefix ('that/of') + להם. Candidates for הם: H1992 'they/them'. Chose H1992 as possessive: 'of them / theirs', referring to the nets belonging to the fishermen.
textual_notes: אספו has no candidates; root אסף ('to gather/collect') is standard Hebrew. The form is 3rd person plural past: 'they gathered'.
משתברין has no candidates; root שבר ('to break') in hitpael/nitpael participial form with Aramaic-influenced ין- ending: 'were breaking / being torn apart'.
באותן — ב + אותן ('in those') is a later Hebrew demonstrative form. No Strong's candidates given.
שרשתות — ש prefix ('that') + רשתות ('nets'). The construct is somewhat unusual; it could be 'so that the nets' (result clause) or 'such that their nets'.

verses.literal: And when this was done they gathered fish many in those nets that theirs [were] breaking

verses.translation: And they signaled [or: made a sign] to [their] companions who were in the other boat, that they should come. And they came and filled all the boats with fish, to such an extent [or: in such a way] that they nearly sank

translation_notes: ועשו (W-ʿ-S-W): The candidate H6215 'Esau' is a proper name and makes no sense here. The consonants are clearly waw + 3mp past of עשה ('to do/make'): 'and they made/did'.
אל (ʾ-L): Candidates: H408 'not', H410 'God/mighty', H413 'to/toward'. Chose H413 because signaling 'to/toward' companions is the coherent action.
אשר: H834 'who/which' — relative pronoun linking companions to their location in the other boat.
באופן (B-ʾ-W-P-N): H212 'wheel'. However, in later Hebrew באופן functions as 'in a manner/way' (derived from the wheel concept of 'turning/mode'). Context requires 'in such a way that'.
שכמעט: ש prefix + כמעט. H4592 'a little/almost'. Chose H4592 because כמעט means 'almost/nearly' — 'they nearly sank'.
לא: H3808 'not' — combined with כמעט: 'almost did not sink' meaning 'they nearly sank' (litotes, or: they almost didn't [stay afloat]).
textual_notes: ועשו — while H6215 'Esau' shares these consonants, the narrative context absolutely requires the verb 'and they made/did'.
באופן — H212 'wheel' is the classical meaning, but in medieval/late Hebrew this became an adverbial expression 'in a manner/way'. The text appears to be in later Hebrew register.

לא נטבעו — 'they did not sink' combined with שכמעט 'that almost': the meaning is 'they almost sank' (i.e., they almost did not [remain afloat], or more naturally: so much fish that they nearly sank). The Hebrew syntax שכמעט לא נטבעו literally reads 'that almost not they-sank', meaning 'they nearly sank'.
נטבעו has no candidates; root טבע means 'to sink/be submerged' (cf. H2883).

verses.literal: And they made a sign to the companions who [were] in the boat the other that they would come and they came and filled all the boats with fish in [a] manner that almost not they sank

verses.translation: And because of this matter [or: event], when Shimon Kepha [saw] Yeshua the Anointed One [or: Messiah], [he fell] at his feet [and said]: Lord, depart [or: separate yourself] please from me, for I am a sinful man
words: to his feet / at his feet

translation_notes: הדבר (H-D-B-R): Candidates: H1907 'vizier', H1697 'word/matter/thing'. Chose H1697 because 'from that matter/event' makes sense as 'because of that happening'.
כאשר: H834 'when' — temporal clause.
שמעון: H8095 'Shimon' preferred over H4583 'abode' or H5771 'perversity' because it is a personal name in context alongside Kepha.
משיח (M-Sh-Y-Ch): Candidates: H4899 'anointed/Messiah', H7878 'to ponder', H7879 'contemplation', H7880 'shrub'. Chose H4899 because it follows the name Yeshua as a title: 'Yeshua the Anointed One'.
אדון (ʾ-D-W-N): Candidates: H113 'sovereign/lord', H114 'Addon (name)'. Chose H113 because Shimon is addressing someone with reverence.
הפרד (H-P-R-D): Candidates: H6504 'to separate/spread apart', H6505 'a mule'. Chose H6504 because 'separate yourself from me' is the coherent plea in this context.
נא (N-ʾ): Candidates: H4994 'please/I pray', H4995 'raw flesh', H4996 'Thebes'. Chose H4994 because it is an interjection added to an imperative.
כי: H3588 'for/because' — introducing the reason for his plea.
textual_notes: וכיפא has no Strong's candidates — it is an Aramaic proper name (Kepha/Cephas, meaning 'rock'), used as a surname for Shimon.
]ראה[, ]נפל[, ]ואמר[ are all bracketed in the source, indicating they are editorial restorations or uncertain readings. The narrative logic strongly supports 'saw', 'fell', and 'said'.

מעלי — מ (from) + על (upon) + י (me). The candidates listed are for עלי; H5941 'Eli' (name) and H5940 'pestle' don't fit. The reading is simply the prepositional phrase 'from upon me' = 'away from me'.
חוטא has no candidates listed; it is a qal active participle of חטא ('to sin'), meaning 'sinner / one who sins'.

verses.literal: And from that the matter when Shimon Kepha [saw] Yeshua Messiah [he fell] to his feet [and said] Lord separate please from upon me for a sinner I [am]

verses.translation: For trembling [or: dread] was surrounding [or: encompassing] him and all those who were with him, because of the catch of fish that they had taken
words: at the catching / in the taking of

translation_notes: כי: H3588 'for/because' — causal conjunction explaining why Shimon said what he said.

חרד (Ch-R-D): Candidates: H2729 'to shudder with terror/fear', H2730 'fearful/reverential'. Chose H2729 because the verbal/adjectival sense of 'trembling/shuddering' better captures the active state described.
הוא (first): H1931 'he' — subject pronoun. The trembling was upon him.
הוא (second): H1931 'he/it' — this second הוא may be emphatic or resumptive, reinforcing that the trembling 'it' was surrounding 'him'.
textual_notes: מסובב has no candidates; root סבב ('to surround/encompass'). The form is pual or polel participle: 'surrounding/encompassing'. The syntax 'trembling he surrounding he' is awkward — likely means 'trembling was surrounding him' with הוא used both for subject (trembling) and object reference.
The double הוא is syntactically unusual. One reading: 'For trembling — it was surrounding him.' Another: 'For trembling he was, surrounded, he and all those...' The first reading seems more natural.
בלקיחת — no candidates; ב + לקיחה + ת (construct): 'at/in the catching of'. From root לקח ('to take/catch').

verses.literal: For trembling he [was] surrounding him and all those that were with him at [the] catching of the fish that they caught

verses.translation: And Yaakov and Yochanan, sons of Zavdi [or: Zebedee], his companions, were standing astonished [or: stunned]. And Yeshua said to Shimon: Do not be afraid, for because of this [or: from now on] you will be a catcher [or: taker] of men — [they will be] with you, in your following [or: under your charge, in your discipleship]
words: in your obedience / under your charge

translation_notes: בני (B-N-Y): Candidates: H1137 'Bani (name)', H1138 'Bunni (name)'. Neither fits; the consonants are clearly the construct plural of בן ('son'): 'sons of'. This is a standard construct form without its own Strong's number.
זבדי: H2067 'Zabdi' — proper name, father of Yaakov and Yochanan (Zebedee in other traditions).
אמר: H559 'to say' — introduces direct speech.
לשמעון: H8095 'Shimon' — the addressee.
אל (ʾ-L): Candidates: H408 'not (deprecative)', H410 'God/mighty', H413 'to/toward'. Chose H408 because אל + imperfect (תפחד) forms a negative command: 'do not fear'.
כי: H3588 'for/because' — introduces the reason not to fear.
בעבור: H5668 'on account of / in order that' — Chose H5668 over H5669 'stored grain' because it introduces purpose/cause.
זה: H2088 'this' — demonstrative pronoun referring to the miraculous catch.
textual_notes: חבירו — no candidates; חבר means 'companion/associate/partner'. The singular suffix ו ('his') with what appears to be a reference to multiple people (Yaakov and Yochanan) suggests 'his companions' with the suffix distributive or the noun understood as collective.
עומדין — no candidates; participle plural of עמד with Aramaic-influenced ין- ending: 'standing'.

שוממין — no candidates; could be from שמם ('to be desolate/astonished/stunned'). The ין- ending again suggests Aramaic influence. In context, 'astonished/stunned' fits the reaction to the miraculous catch.
תפחד — no candidates; root פחד ('to fear/dread'). 2ms imperfect: 'you will fear' → with אל: 'do not fear'.
תהיה — no candidates; root היה, 2ms imperfect: 'you will be'.
לוקח — no candidates; active participle of לקח ('to take/catch'). 'One who catches/takes' — here 'a catcher of men'.

במשמעתך — no candidates; ב + משמעת + ך. The noun משמעת from root שמע ('to hear/obey') means 'obedience/discipline/charge/following'. The suffix is 2ms 'your'. The phrase could mean 'in your following/discipleship' or 'under your authority/charge'. This is an unusual addition suggesting that the people will follow under Shimon's leadership.

verses.literal: And Yaakov and Yochanan sons of Zavdi his companions standing astonished and Yeshua said to Shimon do not fear for on account of this you will be catching men with you in your obedience

verses.translation: And when they had guided the boats to shore, they abandoned all their concerns [or: occupations, matters] and followed after Yeshua the Anointed One. And further, behold —

translation_notes: וכאשר (אשר): Candidates: H833 'to be straight', H834 'who/which/when', H835 'happiness', H836 'Asher', H837 'happiness', H838 'a step'. With prefixed ו+כ, this forms 'and when/as' — chose H834 because כאשר is a temporal conjunction meaning 'when'.
משיח: Candidates: H4899 'anointed/Messiah', H7878 'to ponder', H7879 'contemplation', H7880 'shrubbery'. Following the proper name Yeshua, 'anointed one' is the coherent reading as a title.

והלאה: Candidates: H1973 'to the distance/onward', H3811 'to tire/be disgusted', H3812 'Leah'. In context of a transitional phrase between narrative sections, 'onward/further' (H1973) makes sense as a narrative marker.
textual_notes: אחרי is listed only as H317 'other' in candidates, but the consonants אחרי more naturally read as the preposition 'after/behind' (H310). The context of following a person strongly supports 'after' rather than 'other'.
האףניות appears to be a later Hebrew or loan word for 'boats/ships' not in the standard Strong's lexicon. The consonants suggest אניות (ships) with an inserted ף possibly as a scribal artifact.
והלאה ראו — unclear whether this means 'and further, behold' (transitioning to next section) or 'and from there on, they saw.' The section break suggests a transitional use.

verses.literal: And when they drove the boats to land they left all their affairs and went after Yeshua [the] Anointed and onward see

verses.translation: And this happened [or: came to pass] when Yeshua the Anointed One was in a certain city, and a certain man came, full of leprosy. And when he saw Yeshua, he fell at his feet and pleaded with him, saying: Lord [or: Master, Sovereign], if you are willing, you are able to make me clean.

translation_notes: וזה: Candidates: H2088 'this', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this or that'. With ו prefix, 'and this' makes contextual sense as the opening of a narrative section. H2089 'sheep' would be nonsensical here.
היה: Candidates: H1961 'to exist/be/become', H1962 'ruin', H3050 'Yah'. 'Was' (H1961) is the obvious choice as a copula verb describing Yeshua's location.

בעיר: Candidates: H1165 'cattle', H5892 'a city', H5893 'Ir (name)', H5894 'watcher/angel', H5895 'donkey colt'. 'In a city' (H5892) fits — a person full of leprosy coming to someone in a city is coherent; 'in cattle' or 'in a donkey colt' is not.

אדם: Candidates: H119 'flush/rosy', H120 'human being', H121 'Adam', H122 'rosy', H123 'Edom', H124 'redness/ruby'. H120 'a human being/man' is the natural reading in a narrative about someone approaching Yeshua.
אחד: Candidates: H258 'to unify', H259 'one/first'. H259 'one/a certain' — standard usage as an indefinite article.

מלא: Candidates: H4390 'to fill', H4391 'to fill', H4392 'full', H4393 'fullness', H4394 'consecration', H3808 'not'. H4392 'full' as an adjective describing the man's state with leprosy produces the clearest image.
ראה: Candidates: H7200 'to see', H7201 'vulture', H7202 'seeing/experiencing', H7203 'seer/vision', H7204 'Roeh'. H7200 'he saw' — a verb in context of 'when he saw Yeshua he fell'.
נפל: Candidates: H5307 'to fall', H5308 'to fall', H5309 'abortion'. H5307 'he fell' — falling at someone's feet is a coherent physical image of supplication.
ואומר: Listed only as H201 'Omar (proper name)'. However, the consonants אמר are clearly the verb 'to say' (H559) in participial form with ו prefix. The participial form 'saying' fits the narrative.
אדון: Candidates: H113 'sovereign/controller', H114 'Addon (name)'. H113 'Lord/Master' — a form of address to Yeshua in a plea.
אם: Candidates: H517 'mother', H518 'if/whether'. H518 'if' — introduces a conditional clause in the plea.
אתה: Candidates: H857 'to arrive', H858 'to arrive', H859 'you'. H859 'you' — the subject pronoun in 'you are able'.

verses.literal: And this was done when Yeshua [the] Anointed was in a city one and came a man one full [of] leprosy and when he saw Yeshua he fell to his feet and entreated him and saying Lord if you desire you [are] able to cleanse me

verses.translation: And Yeshua touched him and said: I am willing [or: I desire] — be cleansed! And at once [or: immediately, from hand] the leprosy fled from him.

translation_notes: ואמר: Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 'to say', H561 'something said', H562 'something said', H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer'. H559 'and he said' — standard narrative verb in context of speech following an action.
אני: Candidates: H589 'I', H590 'a ship/fleet'. H589 'I' — the speaker is responding to the leper's plea, so the first-person pronoun is coherent.
לטהר: Candidates: H2891 'to be pure/cleanse', H2892 'brightness/purification'. H2891 as an infinitive 'to cleanse' — directly parallels the leper's request.
ומיד: The candidates list יד H3027 'hand'. With prefix ו+מ, this reads 'and from hand' i.e. 'immediately' — a common idiomatic use.

ברחה: Listed candidate is H7347 'millstone' (רחה). However, the consonants ברח more naturally parse as ברח (H1272 'to flee/run away') with feminine suffix ה for agreement with צרעת (feminine noun). 'The leprosy fled' is a vivid, coherent image; 'the leprosy millstoned' is not.
textual_notes: ברחה — the candidate listed is רחה H7347 'millstone', but the consonants far more naturally read as the verb ברח 'to flee' (H1272) with 3fs suffix. I read it as the latter based on contextual coherence.

verses.literal: And Yeshua touched him and said I desire to cleanse you and immediately the leprosy fled from him

verses.translation: And Yeshua commanded that they should not report [or: tell] it to any person, but he said to him: Go and present yourself to the priests, and make an offering [or: vow] on behalf of your purification, just as Moses commands, as a testimony for them.

translation_notes: אבל: Candidates: H56 'to bewail', H57 'lamenting', H58 'meadow', H59 'Abel (place)', H60 'lamentation', H61 'nay/truly/yet'. H61 'but/yet' — an adversative conjunction between the negative command and the positive instruction.
אמר: Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 'to say', H561 'something said', H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer'. H559 'he said' — narrative speech verb.
אדם: H120 'a human being' — 'to any person' is the natural reading after 'that not they tell it'.

לשום: Candidates: H7760 'to put/set', H7761 'to put', H7762 'garlic'. Here לשום functions as 'to any' — a later Hebrew usage meaning 'any' (from שום 'to set/place' used idiomatically). This fits the prohibition context.

שמשה: Candidates under משה: H4871 'to pull out', H4872 'Moses', H4873 'Moses', H4874 'a debt'; under שה: H7716 'a sheep/goat'. With prefix ש (relative 'that/which'), שמשה = 'that Moses' — H4872 is the coherent reading as 'as Moses commands'.

מצוה: Candidates: H4687 'a command/the Law', H6680 'to command/enjoin'. Could be noun 'command' or verb 'commands'. In context 'as Moses commands' (verb), H6680 as a participle makes the sentence flow naturally.
בעד: H1157 'on behalf of/for' — used with 'your purification' to indicate the purpose of the offering.
בעדות: H5715 'testimony' — with prefix ב, 'for a testimony'.
שלהם: Candidates: H3859 'to rankle', H1990 'Ham', H1991 'abundance', H1992 'they/them'. With prefix ש+ל, this is 'that of them' / 'theirs' — H1992 'them' with prefix ש+ל gives 'of them / for them'.
textual_notes: ותדור could be parsed as from נדר (to vow/make a vow) or דור (to dwell/go around). In context of priestly cleansing ritual, 'vow/offer' makes more sense than 'dwell'.
טהףרתך contains an unexpected ף; likely a scribal variant or error for טהרתך (your purification, H2893).

לרפא: Candidates: H7495 'to cure/heal', H7496 'ghost', H7497 'giant', H7498 'Rapha'. H7495 — infinitive 'to heal' is the only coherent reading with 'the power of YHWH was in him to ___'.

translation_notes: הוא (consonants הוא): Candidates: H1931 'he/she/it', H1932 (Aramaic 'he'), H1933 'to be', H1934 'to exist'. Chose H1931 because this is a pronoun in the question 'who is he this' — a standard Hebrew identificatory clause.

זה (consonants זה): Candidates: H2088 'this/that', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this/that'. Chose H2088 because 'who is he this' is a natural demonstrative question; 'who is he a sheep' makes no sense here.

לבד (consonants לבד): Candidates: H905 'separation/alone', H906 'linen', H907 'a lie'. Chose H905 because 'alone the God' = 'God alone' fits the theological context of exclusive divine prerogative.

האל (consonants האל): Candidates: H408/409 'not', H410 'God/mighty', H411/412 'these/those', H413 'to/near'. Chose H410 with the article: 'the God' — the statement is about who alone can forgive sins.

This is a common verb (H2803 חשב 'to think, plan, reckon') not listed among the candidates. I read it as the infinitive of חשב 'to think.'

translation_notes: משתה (consonants משתה): Candidates: H4960 'a banquet/feast', H4961 'a banquet', or from שתה H8354 'to drink'. Chose H4960 because 'he made a feast' is the natural construction — עשה משתה is a standard Hebrew idiom.
שם (consonants שם): Chose H8033 'there' — locative adverb.

ושאר (consonants שאר): Candidates: H7603 'yeast', H7604 'to swell/be redundant', H7605 'a remainder', H7606 (Aramaic remainder), H7607 'flesh/kindred'. Chose H7605 'remainder/rest' because 'many worldly ones and the rest/others' describes the mixed crowd at the feast.
textual_notes: עולמיים: This term (from עולם 'world/age') in this context appears to designate 'worldly people' or 'people of the world' — those outside the religious establishment. This is a later Hebrew coinage not in classical biblical Hebrew.
The subject of ואוכלים is ambiguous — it could be the worldly ones and others eating with Yeshua's group, or Yeshua and disciples eating with the worldly ones. Context suggests mutual dining.

verses.literal: And he made a feast great in his house and there were there many worldly-ones and others and eating with them

verses.translation: And the Pharisees [separated ones] and the scribes were grumbling [or: complaining] and saying to the disciples of Yeshua the Anointed One [Messiah], Why are you eating and drinking with the worldly people and with the sinners?

translation_notes: משיח (consonants משיח): Candidates: H4899 'anointed/Messiah', or from שיח H7878 'to ponder/converse', H7879 'utterance', H7880 'shrub'. Chose H4899 because 'Yeshua the Anointed One' is a title following the proper name — 'Yeshua the shrub' or 'Yeshua the utterance' produce incoherent images.
למה (consonants ל + מה): Candidates: H4100 'what/why/how', H4101 (Aramaic). Chose H4100 — the interrogative 'why?' introducing the accusatory question.

עם (first occurrence, consonants עם): Candidates: H5971 'a people/tribe', H5972 (Aramaic), H5973 'with', H5974 (Aramaic 'with'). Chose H5973 because 'eating and drinking with the worldly ones' requires the preposition 'with.'
ועם (consonants עם): Same analysis — H5973 'and with' as preposition before 'the sinners.'
textual_notes: אתם: The only candidate given is H864 'Etham (a place).' However, the consonants clearly represent the second person plural pronoun אתם 'you' — standard Hebrew. No Strong's number is typically assigned for basic pronouns in some systems.
העולמיים and החוטאים appear as two distinct groups — 'the worldly ones' and 'the sinners.' Whether these are truly distinct categories or overlapping descriptions is unclear from context alone.

verses.literal: And the separated-ones and the scribes complaining and saying to [the] disciples of Yeshua anointed-one why are you eating and drinking with the worldly-ones and with the sinners

verses.translation: Yeshua responded and said to them: The one who is healthy [or: whole, robust] does not need a healer [or: physician].

translation_notes: ענה (consonants ע-נ-ה): Candidates: H6030 'to respond/answer', H6031 'to depress/afflict', H6032 Aramaic 'to respond', H6034 proper name. Chose H6030 because the immediate context 'answered... and said' is a standard response formula.
ואמר (consonants א-מ-ר): Candidates: H559 'to say', H561 'something said', H563 'a lamb'. Chose H559 because this is clearly a speaking verb coordinated with 'answered.'
להם: Could be H3859 'to rankle' or ל + הם H1992 'to them'. Chose ל + H1992 because the context requires a dative recipient of speech.
שהוא (consonants ה-ו-א): Candidates: H1931 pronoun 'he', H1933 'to be/exist'. Chose H1931 as the relative clause 'who he [is] healthy' uses the pronoun as copula.
textual_notes: אינו, צריך, and רופא have no Strong's candidates listed. These appear to be post-biblical Hebrew forms: אינו = 'he is not' (אין + pronominal suffix), צריך = 'needing/requiring', רופא = active participle of רפא 'to heal' (cf. H7495). They function clearly in context.

verses.literal: Answered Yeshua and said to them not needing [a] healer [is] who he [is] healthy

verses.translation: But [or: rather] the sick need a healer [or: physician], for I did not come to call the righteous — only [to call] sinners to repentance [or: returning, turning back].

translation_notes: אבל (consonants א-ב-ל): Candidates: H56 'bewail', H57 'lamenting', H58 'meadow', H61 'nay/truly/yet'. Chose H61 because the adversative 'but/rather' logically contrasts the healthy not needing a physician with the sick who do.
כי (consonants כ-י): Candidates: H3587 'brand/scar', H3588 conjunction. Chose H3588 because this introduces a causal clause explaining the preceding statement.
אני (consonants א-נ-י): Candidates: H589 'I', H590 'ship/fleet'. Chose H589 because the speaker is identifying himself as the subject of 'came.'
רק (consonants ר-ק): Candidates: H7534 'emaciated', H7535 'only/merely', H7536 'spittle'. Chose H7535 because 'only/merely' creates the logical restriction: not the righteous, only sinners.
לתשובה (consonants ת-ש-ו-ב-ה): H8666 'recurrence/reply/return'. In context, 'returning' (i.e., repentance — turning back) fits the call to sinners.
textual_notes: באתי has no Strong's match listed. The consonants ב-א-ת-י correspond to the first-person perfect of בוא (H935 'to come/go in'). The candidate H863 'Ittai' is a proper name and does not fit.

החולים, צריכים, רופא, לקרוא, הצדיקים, לחוטאים have no Strong's candidates listed. These are standard Hebrew forms: חולים = sick ones (from חלה H2470), צריכים = needing, רופא = healer (from רפא H7495), לקרוא = to call (from קרא H7121), הצדיקים = the righteous (from צדיק H6662), לחוטאים = to sinners (from חטא H2398).

verses.literal: But the sick [ones] need [a] healer for I not came to call the righteous only to sinners to repentance

verses.translation: And they said to him: Why do the disciples of Yochanan [John] fast continually and offer weighty [or: heavy, earnest] prayers, and likewise those of the Pharisees, but yours eat and drink?

translation_notes: והם (consonants ה-ם): Candidates: H1990 'Ham (place)', H1991 'abundance', H1992 'they'. Chose H1992 because the context requires a pronoun subject for 'said.'
למה (consonants מ-ה): H4100 'what/why'. The prefix ל makes this 'for what?' = 'why?'
וכן (consonants כ-ן): Candidates: H3651 'so/thus', H3652 'so' (Aramaic), H3653 'stand/pedestal', H3654 'gnat'. Chose H3651 because 'and so/likewise' connects the Pharisees' disciples to Yochanan's.
אבל (consonants א-ב-ל): Chose H61 'but/yet' because the adversative introduces the contrast with 'yours eat and drink.'
שלך (consonants ש-ל-ך): Candidates: H7993 'to throw', H7994 'pelican'. Neither fits. In post-biblical Hebrew, שלך = 'yours' (possessive pronoun). Context demands 'yours [i.e., your disciples].'

מלחמות: The listed candidate H2545 'mother-in-law' (חמות) does not fit. The word מלחמות could derive from לחם, but in this context — paired with כובד (weight/heaviness) and describing pious activity alongside fasting — this likely represents 'prayers' (a Hebraized form reflecting supplication/intercession). The standard biblical meaning 'battles/wars' would create a bizarre image when combined with 'making weight of wars' in a context about fasting and piety. 'Heavy prayers' is coherent.
כובד: No Strong's candidates listed directly. The consonants כ-ב-ד relate to כבד (H3515 'heavy/weighty'). The noun form means 'weight/heaviness.'
textual_notes: מלחמות is ambiguous. Biblical Hebrew מלחמות means 'wars/battles' (from לחם H3898). However, in this context of fasting and devotional practice, 'battles' makes little sense alongside 'making weight of.' This Hebrew manuscript text may use מלחמות to render a concept of 'prayers/supplications' — possibly a Hebraization of a term for prayer. Alternatively, כובד מלחמות could mean 'heavy struggles/wrestlings' as a metaphor for intense prayer. The reading 'earnest prayers' fits the context best but is uncertain.
תלמידי and מהפרושים have no Strong's candidates. תלמידי = 'disciples of' (post-biblical Hebrew), מהפרושים = 'from the Pharisees' (מן + הפרושים).
שלך as 'yours' is a post-biblical Hebrew possessive, not matching either Strong's candidate (H7993/H7994).

verses.literal: And they said to him why [do] disciples of Yochanan fast continually and make weight of prayers and so those from the Pharisees but yours eat and drink

verses.translation: And he said to them: Are you able to make the sons [or: companions] of the bridegroom fast while the bridegroom is with them?

translation_notes: ולהם: ו + ל + הם. Chose H1992 'them' with preposition ל 'to'. H3859 'to rankle' does not fit the discourse context.
אמר (consonants א-מ-ר): Candidates: H559 'to say', H561 'something said', H563 'lamb'. Chose H559 because the subject is speaking in response.

עשות (consonants ע-ש-ו-ת): Candidates: H6219 'shining/polished', H6220 proper name. Neither fits perfectly. This is the infinitive construct of עשה (H6213 'to do/make'), which shares consonants ע-ש-ה. The ות ending marks the infinitive construct. Context demands 'to make/cause.'
שבני: ש + בני. The ש is the relative particle 'that.' בני candidates: H1137/H1138 proper names, or בני as construct plural of בן (H1121 'son'). Context requires 'sons of' the bridegroom.
בעוד (consonants ע-ו-ד): Candidates: H5749 'to testify', H5750 'continuance/still/while', H5751 same. Chose H5750 because ב + עוד = 'while still' describing the temporal condition.
textual_notes: אתם: The listed candidate H864 'Etham (a place)' does not fit. This is the second-person plural pronoun 'you' (standard Hebrew).
הארוס has no Strong's entry. This is a post-biblical Hebrew term for 'bridegroom/betrothed one' (from ארס 'to betroth').
יצומו and יכולים have no Strong's entries listed. יצומו = 'they will fast' from צום (H6684), יכולים = 'able' from יכל (H3201).

verses.literal: And to them said [are you] able you to make that sons of the bridegroom will fast while that the bridegroom [is] with them

verses.translation: But days will come when the bridegroom will be separated [or: taken away] from them, and then they will fast in those days.

translation_notes: אבל (consonants א-ב-ל): Chose H61 'but/yet' as it introduces the contrasting future scenario.

כאשר (consonants א-ש-ר): Candidates: H833 'to be straight', H834 'who/which/when', H835 'happiness', H836 'Asher', H837 'happiness', H838 'step'. Chose H834 with כ prefix = 'as/when', introducing the temporal clause.
מהם (consonants ה-ם): Candidates: H1990 'Ham', H1991 'abundance', H1992 'they'. Chose H1992 with מן prefix = 'from them', as the bridegroom is separated from the companions.
textual_notes: יבואו, ימים, יפרד, יצומו, באותן, הימים lack Strong's candidates. יבואו = 'they will come' (from בוא H935), ימים = 'days' (from יום H3117), יפרד = 'will be separated' (from פרד H6504), יצומו = 'will fast' (from צום H6684), באותן = 'in those' (post-biblical demonstrative), הימים = 'the days.'

verses.literal: But will come days when the bridegroom will be separated from them and then they will fast in those the days

verses.translation: And [I am] telling you a parable: No person exchanges [or: patches] a new garment with an old garment, for if he does so, the old is torn [or: broken], and the new does not unite [or: match] with the old.

translation_notes: ואומר: The candidate H201 'Omar' (proper name) does not fit. This is the active participle of אמר (H559) with ו prefix = 'and [I am] saying/telling.'

משל (consonants מ-ש-ל): Candidates: H4910 'to rule', H4911 'to use figurative language', H4912 'parable/maxim', H4913 place name, H4914 'satire', H4915 'empire'. Chose H4912 because the speaker explicitly introduces a figurative illustration.

שום (consonants ש-ו-ם): Candidates: H7760 'to put/set', H7762 'garlic'. Here שום אדם = 'any man / no man' (in combination with לא), a standard post-biblical Hebrew construction using שום as an indefinite determiner.
אדם (consonants א-ד-ם): Candidates: H120 'human being', H121 'Adam', H123 'Edom'. Chose H120 because the context describes any person generically.

מלבוש (consonants מ-ל-ב-ו-ש): H4403 'garment/clothing'. The alternative readings H3830 (לבוש 'garment') or H954 (בוש 'to be ashamed') — chose H4403 as the full form including the מ prefix fits 'garment.'
חדש (consonants ח-ד-ש): Candidates: H2318 'to be new/rebuild', H2319 'new', H2320 'new moon/month'. Chose H2319 'new' as adjective modifying garment.
ישן (consonants י-ש-ן): Candidates: H3462 'to sleep', H3463 'sleepy', H3465 'old'. Chose H3465 'old' because it describes the garment's age, contrasting with 'new.'
כי אם: H3588 + H518 = 'for if' — a conditional causal clause.
עם (consonants ע-ם): Candidates: H5971 'people', H5973 'with'. Chose H5973 because the new does not unite 'with' the old.
textual_notes: יחליף has no Strong's candidates listed. From חלף (H2498 'to pass on, change, exchange'). The hiphil form means 'to exchange/replace.'
נשבר has no candidates listed. From שבר (H7665 'to break/burst'). The niphal 'is broken/torn.'
מתיחד has no candidates listed. This appears to be a hitpael form from יחד (H3161 'to be united'). 'Does not unite itself / does not match.'

The parable's logic: putting a new garment patch on an old one ruins the old and the new doesn't match. The verb יחליף could mean 'patch' rather than simply 'exchange' — both are possible from the consonants.

verses.literal: And saying to you [a] parable no man not exchanges garment new with garment old for if he does it the old [is] torn and new not does unite with the old

verses.translation: And no person has [the right] to put new wine into an old wineskin, for if he does so, the new wine bursts [or: breaks] the old wineskins, and the skins are destroyed and the wine is spilled out.

translation_notes: ושום (consonants ש-ו-ם): H7760 'to put/set'. Here as indefinite 'any' (ושום אדם אין = 'and no person').
אדם: Chose H120 'human being' — generic person in a parable.
אין (consonants א-י-ן): Candidates: H369 'non-entity/negative particle', H370 'where?', H371 'is it not?'. Chose H369 as the negation 'there is not.'
לשום: ל + שום. H7760 'to put' with ל infinitive marker = 'to put.'
חדש: H2319 'new' — adjective for wine.
בנאד: ב + נאד H4997 'in a skin bag.'
ישן: H3465 'old' — describing the wineskin.

משבר (consonants מ-ש-ב-ר): Candidates: H4866 'orifice of womb', H4867 'breaker of the sea', or from שבר H7665 'to burst/break'. Chose H7665 in participial/causative form because the new wine 'breaks/bursts' the old skins — a coherent physical image of fermentation pressure.
כי אם: H3588 + H518 = 'for if.'
textual_notes: משבר: Could be read as the noun H4867 'breaker' or as a verbal form from שבר H7665 'to break.' The participial reading 'breaking/bursting' fits the active image of wine breaking skins.
אובדין has no Strong's entry. This is a post-biblical/Aramaic-influenced plural participle from אבד (H6 'to perish/be destroyed').
נשפך has no candidates listed. From שפך (H8210 'to pour out'). Niphal = 'is poured out/spilled.'
הנאדות, והנאדות: Plural of נאד (H4997) with feminine plural ending = 'the wineskins.'

verses.literal: And no man there is not to him to put wine new in [a] skin old for if he does it the wine new bursts the skins the old and the skins perish and the wine is poured out

verses.translation: But new wine is fitting [or: proper] to put into a new wineskin, and [both] the wine and the skins are preserved [or: sustained, endure together].

translation_notes: אבל: Chose H61 'but/rather' as it contrasts the right method with the wrong one described previously.
חדש: H2319 'new' — adjective for both wine and skin.
לשים: ל + שים. The candidates for ים include H3220 'sea' etc., but this is clearly the infinitive of שים/שום (H7760 'to put') with ל prefix. The ים is part of the verb root, not the suffix.
בנאד: ב + H4997 'in a skin bag.'
textual_notes: ראוי has no Strong's entry. This is a post-biblical Hebrew adjective meaning 'fitting/worthy/proper' (from ראה H7200 'to see' — literally 'seen as fit').
מתקיימין has no Strong's entry. This is a hitpael participle with Aramaic-influenced plural ending from קום (H6965 'to stand/arise'). The meaning is 'are sustained/preserved/endure.'

verses.literal: But wine new fitting to put in [a] skin new and the wine and the skins are preserved

verses.translation: And no person [who is] drinking old wine wants immediately to drink new wine, for he says: The old — it is good [or: better, pleasant].

translation_notes: ושום: H7760 used as indefinite determiner 'any' — ושום אדם = 'and any/no person.'
אדם: H120 'human being' — generic person.
ישן (consonants י-ש-ן): H3465 'old' — describing the wine.
מיד (consonants מ-י-ד): From מן + יד H3027 'hand'. The idiomatic meaning 'from the hand' = 'immediately/at once.'
חדש: H2319 'new' — adjective for wine.
כי: H3588 conjunction 'for/because.'
אומר: The candidate H201 'Omar' (proper name) does not fit. This is the participle of אמר H559 'saying/says.'
הישן: H3465 'the old' — with article, referring to old wine.
הוא (consonants ה-ו-א): Candidates: H1931 pronoun 'he/it', H1933 'to be'. Chose H1931 as the copular pronoun: 'the old — it [is] good.'
טוב (consonants ט-ו-ב): Candidates: H2895 'to be good', H2896 'good (adj/noun)', H2897 place name, H2898 'goodness'. Chose H2896 as the predicate adjective 'good.'

רוצה has no Strong's entry listed. From רצה (H7521 'to be pleased with/accept') — the participle means 'wanting/desiring.'
שתות has no Strong's entry listed. This is the infinitive construct of שתה (H8354 'to drink').
